text.p: Swedish debt yields fell on Friday after key U.S. August jobs data was stronger than expected.
"We traded yields higher ahead of the payroll figures but after they were released the market showed renewed strength," a dealer said.
The nine-year bond yield dropped four baisis points to 8.13 percent while the six month T-bill rate fell by four basis points to 5.01 percent.
In the morning yields followed a weaker German market and rose several basis points.
Trade, however, was very thin ahead of the U.S. payroll data, which sparked a rise before pushing yields lower.
The crown was mainly unchanged and was quoted at 4.4680 compared to 4.4700 late Thursday.
Next week the Riksbank's inflation survey due on Wednesday and Swedish consumer prices on Thursday will be in focus.
The market was also looking for the French budget on Tuesday and U.S. PPI figures on Thursday.
